summary: Remote-controlled agent exposes local shell, filesystem, and self-upgrade to configured WebSocket server
details: The package runs a long-lived agent process that connects out to a WebSocket server (default ws://localhost:3456, configurable via env/config) and dispatches server-sent messages into privileged local operations on the installer's host. `terminal_create` spawns an interactive shell via node-pty (`process.env.SHELL || 'bash'` on Unix, PowerShell/cmd on Windows); `terminal_input` writes `msg.data` received from the socket directly into the PTY (`term.pty.write(msg.data)` in connection/index.js), giving whoever controls the server arbitrary shell execution. Additional message types perform server-directed file read/write and git push/reset. On receiving an `upgrade_agent` message the agent resolves the latest version of `@yeaft/webchat-agent` from registry.npmjs.org and runs an unpinned `npm install @yeaft/webchat-agent@latest` in a detached script, then restarts itself under systemd / launchd / PM2 — so the same server channel can force the host to fetch and execute any future published version. Access is gated only by a shared AGENT_SECRET; compromise of the configured server or that secret yields full-host RCE on every connected agent. service/linux.js also mutates PATH (~/.local/bin, ~/.npm-global/bin) to make the agent discoverable across shells.
